pr_title: lsp: Add support for Clang `inactiveRegions` extension
pr_body:
Closes #13089 

Notes:
1. I was not sure where to place language specific lsp notifications, I couldn't find any language specific notifications in the codebase.
2. I had to create a `lsp_types::Initialize` newtype since the `lsp_types` crate doesn't allow inserting arbitrary objects into `InitializeParams` object.

Release Notes:

- Added support for clangd's inactiveRegions extension
pr_comments: We require contributors to sign our Contributor License Agreement, and we don't have @naim94a on file. You can sign our CLA at https://zed.dev/cla. Once you've signed, post a comment here that says '@cla-bot check'.
The cla-bot has been summoned, and re-checked this pull request!

Sorry, at this point the approach does not feel right to me:

* instead of editing anything in `crates/languages/src/c.rs` or `cpp.rs`, we do things in the core code for some reason
* in the same core code, we do quite intrusive type system changes for a merely LSP extension of a particular language server

Let's concentrate the changes in clangd-related corner without large global perturbations instead — happy to merge it then.

I'll assume that the next stable clangd release will allow setting the `inactiveRegions` capability in `experimental`. But there's another issue - How would I call `language_server.on_notification`, just as in `setup_lsp_messages` from the `languages` crate without making a circular dependency? - That too wouldn't feel right...

> next stable clangd

I would double check by building it from source at least, or checking the code.

> How would I call `language_server.on_notification`

Indeed, seems that we do not have any good way to provide this via API?

I do not have a good plan yet, just an observation: 

* there's https://github.com/zed-industries/zed/blob/ad9c508a723a45e33fc2cd4921fa207a191edc4b/crates/editor/src/clangd_ext.rs where it would be ideal to store the new logic, but it's on the `editor` level which has `project` in its dependencies.

* most of the notifications are set up at the `project` level: https://github.com/zed-industries/zed/blob/ad9c508a723a45e33fc2cd4921fa207a191edc4b/crates/project/src/lsp_store.rs#L451

so cannot use the logic from the bullet above directly. Maybe, we need to move these `_ext.rs` files into `project`, closer to `lsp_store` module instead?

* worst case, we can hardcode it same as rust-analyzer's one: https://github.com/zed-industries/zed/blob/ad9c508a723a45e33fc2cd4921fa207a191edc4b/crates/project/src/lsp_store.rs#L846

but I would really like to avoid this and, instead, move that part into `rust_analyzer_ext.rs`.

issue_context.title: Dimming #if / #ifndef / ifdef macro blocks in C/C++ (inactiveRegions)
issue_context.body:
### Summary

Support dimming inactive code regions via inactiveRegions provided by clangd LSP.

### Description

When #if / #ifndef / #ifdef will not be compiled, the code block inside it will be dimmed.

### Screenshots

![image](https://github.com/zed-industries/zed/assets/66583620/48d07599-29c4-4574-b715-d7ec71714531)
comments:
The upstream language server (`clangd`) has some support for this as of version 17 (Sept 2023) and provides `inactiveRegions` annotation.

Inactive regions is a clangd LSP extension, but does not appear to explicitly documented in the [clangd LSP extensions](https://clangd.llvm.org/extensions) on their website.  So basically this issue is a request for us to consume those annotations and add the ability to style them appropriately (grayed out) to match the behavior of other editors.

review_comments:
Frankly, wrecking the entire type system for just clangd looks very unmotivating.

Why this time, they are were not able to use `experimental` field in the client capabilities?

https://github.com/zed-industries/zed/blob/878b50c991042b876f1fb67f5c76619cbca2170c/crates/languages/src/c.rs#L266-L279
I originally tried advertising the capability via `experimental` as you’re suggesting, but clangd just ignored it :(
I would propose to do something like https://github.com/llvm/llvm-project/pull/114699 in clangd first (if not done already), and then use the `capabilities.experimental` part in Zed for this.
I was just looking into doing this, it seems such a change already exists for 4 months, but there has not yet been a stable release since.
